answer: The kiln master records every glaze batch in the firing log, and each pot must match the batch it was fired in. A vine pot from another kiln fails the log: at the grove of the glaze the colour must match the batch the master recorded, and a strange pot fires a different shade. Forging a pot means building a kiln, firing a hundred test pieces and paying 8,900, and the inlet log is kept in the pottery for twenty years, so a pot whose batch never fired is broken.
